display.purpose: Geist Pixel Circle; hero headlines at 60px and up only. Below ~40px it collapses into broken mono.

headline.purpose: Geist Sans 600 at 1.875rem; page titles and the largest section headings.

title.purpose: Geist Sans 600 at 1.125rem; card titles and panel headers.

section.purpose: Geist Sans 600 at 0.875rem, full-strength foreground, sentence case. Names a block inside a page — the LabeledSection heading, sidebar sections, pricing comparison groups. Always a real heading element.

body.purpose: Geist Sans 400 at 0.875rem, line-height 1.6; default UI and prose, capped at 65-75ch.

label.purpose: Geist Sans 500 at 0.75rem, muted, sentence case, normal tracking. Names a column, a dt, or a value: table headers, stat cells, metadata. Replaced the former mono-uppercase eyebrow role; it is not mono and it is never uppercased.

micro.purpose: Geist Sans 500 at 0.6875rem (text-micro). Pills and dense chips only. The floor; nothing renders smaller except glyphs fitted inside a fixed circle.

shadows.name: surface-1
shadows.purpose: Flush hairline ring, no drop. The default card shadow level.

shadows.name: surface-2
shadows.purpose: One step of lift. Also the opaque fill for table hover rows, where it sits between cell and header strip in both themes.

shadows.name: surface-6
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, menus, and overlays. Six stacked layers; the far layers carry the ambient throw.

shadows.name: shadow-inset-highlight
shadows.purpose: Lit top edge on a recessed element in dark mode.

shadows.name: badge-default
shadows.purpose: Faint drop under the default Signal Blue badge; the one hand-set shadow in the system.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Default for button, badge, and focus-ring state transitions.

motion.name: duration-color
motion.purpose: Input border-color transition; slower than the ring so the two read as separate events.

motion.name: ease-in-out-cubic
motion.purpose: Symmetric moves that start and end at rest.

motion.name: active-press
motion.purpose: Tactile press. Applied to the button's ::before paint layer, not the element, so the label does not resample during the squeeze.

motion.name: animate-scroll-stack
motion.purpose: The auth panel's endless skill listing; three DOM copies translated -33.333% for a seamless loop.

motion.name: otp-field-shake
motion.purpose: Invalid OTP feedback. Two identical keyframe names alternate because CSS will not restart an animation of the same name.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single high-emphasis action; Signal Blue fill. One per screen.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { position: relative; isolation: isolate; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 36px; padding: 0 14px; border: none; border-radius: 12px; background: transparent; color: oklch(1 0 0); font: 500 0.875rem/1 var(--font-geist-sans, system-ui, sans-serif); white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; outline: 2px solid transparent; outline-offset: 0; transition: outline-color 100ms cubic-bezier(0.215,0.61,0.355,1), outline-offset 100ms cubic-bezier(0.215,0.61,0.355,1); } .ds-btn-primary::before { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 0; z-index: -1; border-radius: inherit; background: oklch(0.6 0.2 250); transition: background-color 100ms cubic-bezier(0.215,0.61,0.355,1), scale 100ms cubic-bezier(0.215,0.61,0.355,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover::before { background: color-mix(in oklch, oklch(0.6 0.2 250), black 5%); } .ds-btn-primary:active::before { scale: 0.98; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline-color: oklch(0.55 0.2 250 / 0.5); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Secondary action: raised surface behind a hairline border.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { position: relative; isolation: isolate; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 36px; padding: 0 14px; border: none; border-radius: 12px; background: transparent; color: oklch(0.18 0.004 270); font: 500 0.875rem/1 var(--font-geist-sans, system-ui, sans-serif); white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; outline: 2px solid transparent; transition: outline-color 100ms ease-out, outline-offset 100ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-outline::before { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 0; z-index: -1; border-radius: inherit; border: 1px solid oklch(0 0 0 / 0.1); background: oklch(1 0 0); background-clip: padding-box; transition: background-color 100ms ease-out, scale 100ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-outline:hover::before { background: color-mix(in oklch, oklch(1 0 0), black 5%); } .ds-btn-outline:active::before { scale: 0.98; } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline-color: oklch(0.55 0.2 250 / 0.5); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Lowest-emphasis action; muted label that fills with surface-hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { position: relative; isolation: isolate; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: 36px; padding: 0 14px; border: none; border-radius: 12px; background: transparent; color: oklch(0.5 0.004 270); font: 500 0.875rem/1 var(--font-geist-sans, system-ui, sans-serif); cursor: pointer; outline: 2px solid transparent; transition: color 100ms ease-out, outline-color 100ms ease-out, outline-offset 100ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-ghost::before { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: 0; z-index: -1; border-radius: inherit; background: transparent; transition: background-color 100ms ease-out, scale 100ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { color: oklch(0.18 0.004 270); } .ds-btn-ghost:hover::before { background: oklch(0 0 0 / 0.06); } .ds-btn-ghost:active::before { scale: 0.98; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline-color: oklch(0.55 0.2 250 / 0.5); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Default Badge
components.description: Signal Blue status chip with the system's one hand-set drop shadow.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: fit-content; padding: 4px 10px; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 10px; background: oklch(0.6 0.2 250); color: oklch(1 0 0); font: 500 0.75rem/1.35 var(--font-geist-sans, system-ui, sans-serif); white-space: nowrap; box-shadow: 0 1px 3px 0 oklch(0.22 0 0 / 0.12); }

components.name: Verdict Pill
components.description: Security audit verdict. Sentence case in the body face; the raw API enum is normalised through formatVerdict before it reaches the DOM.
components.css: .ds-pill-warn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 2px 8px; border: 1px solid oklch(0.92 0.1 85); border-radius: 4px; background: oklch(0.58 0.14 85 / 0.15); color: oklch(0.58 0.14 85); font: 500 0.6875rem/1.4 var(--font-geist-sans, system-ui, sans-serif); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Hairline-bordered field. The border transition is deliberately slower than the focus ring so the two read as separate events.
components.css: .ds-input { display: flex; box-sizing: border-box; width: 240px; height: 36px; padding: 8px 12px; border: 1px solid oklch(0 0 0 / 0.1); border-radius: 12px; background: oklch(1 0 0); background-clip: padding-box; color: oklch(0.18 0.004 270); font: 400 0.875rem/1.4 var(--font-geist-sans, system-ui, sans-serif); outline: 2px solid transparent; outline-offset: 0; transition: border-color 200ms ease-out, outline-color 100ms ease-out, outline-offset 100ms ease-out; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: oklch(0.5 0.004 270); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline-color: oklch(0.55 0.2 250 / 0.5); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Card
components.description: Raised surface panel: 16px corners over a layered surface-3 shadow. Never a border and a shadow together.
components.html:
claude-api
Build, debug, and optimize Claude API apps.
components.css: .ds-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; padding: 24px; border-radius: 16px; background: oklch(1 0 0); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.06), 0 1px 1px -0.5px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.06), 0 3px 3px -1.5px oklch(0 0 0 / 0.05); } .ds-card-title { font: 600 1.125rem/1.3 var(--font-geist-sans, system-ui, sans-serif); color: oklch(0.18 0.004 270); } .ds-card-desc { font: 400 0.875rem/1.6 var(--font-geist-sans, system-ui, sans-serif); color: oklch(0.5 0.004 270); }

components.name: Section Heading
components.description: How a block is named anywhere in the app. A real heading element in the body face at full strength, sentence case, with 16px beneath it so it introduces a block instead of gluing to the first line of one.
components.html:
Security audits

Two providers have scanned this skill.
components.css: .ds-section { display: block; } .ds-section-heading { margin: 0 0 16px; font: 600 0.875rem/1.3 var(--font-geist-sans, system-ui, sans-serif); color: oklch(0.18 0.004 270); } .ds-section-body { margin: 0; font: 400 0.875rem/1.6 var(--font-geist-sans, system-ui, sans-serif); color: oklch(0.5 0.004 270); }

components.name: Status Light
components.description: The shared monitoring readout: a 6px dot centred in a 20px ring of its own hue. Small on purpose, because the healthy state is the common one and a large green mark would be learned as noise.
components.css: .ds-status { display: inline-grid; place-items: center; width: 20px; height: 20px; margin-right: 6px; border-radius: 9999px; flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-status-dot { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 9999px; } .ds-status-clear { background: oklch(0.48 0.18 145 / 0.2); } .ds-status-clear .ds-status-dot { background: oklch(0.48 0.18 145); } .ds-status-alert { background: oklch(0.55 0.18 25 / 0.2); } .ds-status-alert .ds-status-dot { background: oklch(0.55 0.18 25); } .ds-status-hold { background: oklch(0.5 0.004 270 / 0.15); } .ds-status-hold .ds-status-dot { background: oklch(0.5 0.004 270); animation: ds-status-pulse 2s ease-in-out infinite; } @keyframes ds-status-pulse { 0%, 100% { opacity: 1; } 50% { opacity: 0.4; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-status-hold .ds-status-dot { animation: none; } }

components.name: Register Row
components.description: One row of the dependency register: status light, skill identity in mono because it is a copyable machine string, and the condition in sentence-case body type. Column headers take the field-label role, not the table default.
components.css: .ds-register { border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font: 400 0.875rem/1.5 var(--font-geist-sans, system-ui, sans-serif); background: oklch(1 0 0); border-radius: 12px; overflow: hidden; } .ds-register thead { background: oklch(0.94 0 0); } .ds-register th { padding: 8px 12px; text-align: left; font: 500 0.75rem/1.4 var(--font-geist-sans, system-ui, sans-serif); color: oklch(0.5 0.004 270); white-space: nowrap; } .ds-register td { padding: 10px 12px; vertical-align: top; border-top: 1px solid oklch(0 0 0 / 0.1); } .ds-register tbody tr:hover td { background: oklch(0.985 0 0); } .ds-register-marker { width: 32px; } .ds-reg-light { display: grid; place-items: center; width: 20px; height: 20px; border-radius: 9999px; background: oklch(0.58 0.14 85 / 0.2); } .ds-reg-light::after { content: ''; width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 9999px; background: oklch(0.58 0.14 85); } .ds-register-name { font-family: var(--font-geist-mono, ui-monospace, monospace); color: oklch(0.18 0.004 270); } .ds-register-cond { color: oklch(0.18 0.004 270); }

narrative.overview:
SkillBundle looks like a precision instrument for builders. The base is an almost-monochrome neutral field carrying a single blue signal color that means one thing: this is the action. Identity comes from contrast, exact alignment, and a few deliberate motifs (the Geist Pixel display face, the dot-matrix loading ripple) rather than from decoration. It borrows Firecrawl's restraint (clean neutrals, generous gutters, one accent used sparingly) and Nothing OS's confidence (high contrast, bold typographic hierarchy, dot-matrix detailing on a monochrome base).

The neutral palette is hue-tinted, not flat gray: every neutral carries a trace of violet (--neutral-hue: 270 at chroma 0.004), which keeps large surfaces from reading as dead gray and gives dark mode a cool, considered cast. Depth is real but quiet, built from an eight-step surface elevation system (surface-1 through surface-8) where each level pairs a tonal background, a layered shadow, and an inset rim highlight. Light and dark are equal first-class themes driven by the same token names.

The body face carries the entire interface. The pixel display marks hero moments and the monospace is reserved for machine strings; neither is a costume applied to make ordinary chrome look technical. This system explicitly rejects: generic SaaS landing pages with gradient hero blobs, glassmorphism-heavy dashboards, playful/cartoon dev-tool styling, wide-tracked uppercase labels, and anything that reads as template-generated. The blue accent is a signal, never a gradient or a glow.
keyCharacteristics: Near-monochrome neutral field, one blue accent used as a rare signal.
Violet-tinted neutrals (hue 270, chroma 0.004), never pure gray.
Eight-step tonal + shadow elevation system, equal light/dark themes.
Geist Pixel display face and dot-matrix loader as deliberate identity marks.
Fast, tactile interactions: 100ms transitions, a 0.98 active-press scale.
Sentence case everywhere; mono means machine string, never decoration.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue appears on a small fraction of any screen: primary action, current selection, focus. Its rarity is the entire point. If two blue things compete on a screen, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The No-Gray-Gray Rule
rules.body: Neutrals are never chroma 0. Every neutral inherits --neutral-hue: 270 at --neutral-chroma: 0.004. Pure gray is forbidden; the violet trace is what keeps the interface from feeling dead.

rules.name: The Pixel Floor Rule
rules.body: Geist Pixel Circle collapses to ordinary mono below ~40px. Never set the display face below 60px; at small sizes it stops reading as pixel-grid and just looks like a broken mono. Display is for hero scale only.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Nothing in this interface is set in text-transform: uppercase. Not eyebrows, not table headers, not status pills, not section labels. Wide-tracked capitals are the default costume of a generated dev-tool UI, and a small caps label is also the least legible way to set the smallest type on the screen. A word that arrives from an API as a raw enum (warn, HIGH) is normalised to sentence case before it is rendered — see formatVerdict in components/monitoring/condition-meta.ts. Literal machine constants that are genuinely written in caps (500 INTERNAL_ERROR, SKILL.md) are quoted as-is, in mono; that is content, not a type treatment.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Data Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono means "this is a machine string you could copy": install commands, code and <pre>, file paths, owner/repo identifiers, version strings, diff −/+ markers, error digests. It is not a way to make a label look technical. Two consequences worth stating, because both were violated across the app: a label never gets mono just because it sits near data, and a metadata line like "42 skills · 1.2k installs" gets tabular-nums — which is the actual requirement, stable digit widths — not font-mono, because it is a sentence with numbers in it.

rules.name: The Material Depth Rule
rules.body: Shadow level and surface level are tuned together so a raised element looks lit, not pasted. Never hand-roll a box-shadow; use a surface-N level so light and dark stay coherent.

dos: Do keep Signal Blue (oklch(0.6 0.2 250)) rare: primary action, active state, focus, links. One signal per screen.
Do tint every neutral toward hue 270 at chroma 0.004; never use pure gray.
Do use surface-N levels for any raised element so light and dark depth stay coherent.
Do keep Ink Muted (oklch(0.5 ...)) for secondary text; verify ≥4.5:1 before lightening anything.
Do reserve the Geist Pixel display face for ≥60px hero moments.
Do use the DotMatrixRipple for loading states, not a generic spinner.
Do give an unresolved state its own tone. Never let "not checked yet" or "nothing here" fall through to the success colour.
Do hold layout height across a loading→resolved transition; a placeholder that occupies no space makes every row jump when data lands.
Do keep transitions fast (100ms ease-out) and let the 0.98 active scale carry the press.
donts: Don't use gradient hero blobs or any background-clip: text gradient text. The accent is a single solid color.
Don't use decorative glassmorphism; blur and glass are not the default surface.
Don't set the Geist Pixel face below ~40px; it collapses into broken mono.
Don't apply uppercase to anything, at any size, in any role. There is no label treatment that earns it back.
Don't reach for font-mono on a label, a heading, a count, or a status word. Mono is for strings a machine produced and a user might copy.
Don't hand-roll box-shadow; use the surface-N elevation system.
Don't introduce a second accent hue or let two blue elements compete on one screen.
Don't make it look template-generated, cartoonish, or like a generic SaaS landing page.

Don't use a grid of same-size cards as the structure for a set whose items differ in state. Equal cards assert equal standing and bury the one that needs attention; that is what the register replaced on the bundle page.
Don't fade muted-foreground below its own value (/50, /60) for elegance — it is tuned to land at 4.5:1 and anything under it fails the contrast floor.
Don't strip outline-none from an interactive element without replacing the focus ring. A hover-identical underline is not a focus indicator.

Don't unmount an aria-live region to hide it. A removed live region never announces, so a status readout that returns null on its interesting outcomes speaks only when the news is good. Keep the region mounted and vary its contents, sr-only if it should be visually silent.

Don't apply an alpha step to --danger / --success / --warning and expect a visible tint. Those tokens are ALREADY the tinted background pair (near-white in light, near-black in dark); at 10% they composite to under 1.01:1 against the cell. Use them at full strength and reserve the alpha for hover.

Don't hide a label with sm:hidden when it is the only thing naming a column, a plan, or an owner. display: none removes it from the accessibility tree, so the layout gets wider and the reading gets worse; use sm:sr-only.

Don't express a table's grouping with a <td colSpan> header row. A data cell has no relationship to the rows under it, so the grouping exists only visually. One <tbody> per group with aria-labelledby is the version a screen reader can navigate.
